text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parliamentary committee for financial affairs expresses concern at widening public debt and fiscal deficit.
- Leandros Zachariades, Presidential Commissioner for Humanitarian Affairs, dies of cancer.
- Athens believes solution to the Cyprus problem will come in 1998.
- State-run electricity authority is called to pay for a software contract which is 70,000 pounds ($149,000) higher than the next bid.
- The government wants to give a pension to a member of the former EOKA B organisation.
- Foreigners are preparing talks between the two sides on the Cyprus problem by March.
- Scotland Yard detectives go to the occupied areas for investigations in connection with murder of Turkish Cypriot in London.
- Man from Georgia is arrested for attempting to elope with a 16 year old.
- Moscow and Washington are at loggerheads over Russian plans to sell military hardware to Cyprus and American attempts to block any Russian initiative on Cyprus.
- The joint defence pact between Cyprus and Greece cannot be used to deal with political problems, says Greek Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos.
